sources.title: Netflix releases trailer for Brad Bird's Ray Gunn

items.title: Brad Bird's Ray Gunn Started With a Song He Misheard
items.body: Brad Bird's new animated feature, Ray Gunn, comes to Netflix in December, described as a neo-noir science-fiction mystery. Its origin is a case of mistaken identity: Bird has said the film's inspiration came when he heard the opening of the B-52s' 'Planet Claire' — a personal favourite — and initially thought it was a cover of Henry Mancini's theme music from the classic TV show Peter Gunn. He has been kicking the idea around for the last 30 years. Building a noir around a theme you misheard as someone else's theme is a crooked but oddly fitting route into the genre, and December is when we find out what 30 years of it looks like.

sources.title: NASA Selects Far-Infrared Telescope as First in New Mission Class

items.title: NASA's First Probe Explorer Heads Into Preliminary Design
items.body: NASA announced Wednesday that PRIMA — the PRobe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics — is advancing to the next phase of development. It is the first mission in a new class of NASA astrophysics missions, called Probe Explorers, sitting within the agency's longstanding Explorers Program. The selection moves PRIMA into Phase B, the stage that advances preliminary design and technology development for the mission. The acronym doubles as the brief: a probe-class observatory built around far-infrared astrophysics, and the first test of whether the new class delivers.

sources.title: Canada’s proposed labour reforms could shift power away from workers in major disputes

discussion.body: Codify is the word to watch. A Section 107 power wrapped in a formal process becomes easier to treat as routine than as an exception.

Or the bill simply describes the Board's job bluntly: take action to prevent strikes and lockouts, with arbitration as the illustration. That is a broad mandate to hand an industrial relations board, whatever the label on it.

items.title: Bill C-39 Would Put Section 107's Strike-Stopping Power in Writing
items.body: The federal government's newly tabled Bill C-39 would give Ottawa a more direct and explicit role in labour disputes in federally regulated sectors, changing how the government may respond to strikes and lockouts. The mechanism is specific: the bill would codify and structure the federal labour minister's authority under Section 107 of the Canada Labour Code to direct the Canada Industrial Relations Board to take action to prevent strikes and lockouts, including referring a dispute to binding arbitration. The word 'including' is doing quiet work in that sentence. Binding arbitration is the named example of the action the Board may be directed to take, not necessarily the only one — which is why a provision written as a guardrail can read just as easily as an instruction manual.

sources.title: Arctic Sea Ice Reaches 2026 Annual Minimum Extent

items.title: Arctic Sea Ice's 2026 Minimum Ties for 10th-Lowest in the Satellite Record
items.body: NASA reports that Arctic sea ice reached its annual minimum extent on Sept. 12. The ice covered an estimated 1.78 million square miles (4.6 million square kilometres), tying 2008, 2010 and 2025 for the 10th-lowest minimum in the satellite record. The tie is the detail worth holding on to: a shared rank means 2026 lands in a cluster of recent years rather than standing apart from them, and a single season's number is a poor place to look for a verdict either way.
